title: feat(types,components): declare EmptySchema.action as SchemaNode and enforce it
body:
Fixes #7105

Implements option (a) of the ruling on that card (director seat, decision batch #69, 2026-09-07; maintainer reply, verbatim: 「其他同意」). Options (b) and (c) were refused there and are not revisited here.

## The state this ends

`empty` rendered an `action` node and `content/docs/components/feedback/empty.mdx` documented it, while four surfaces disagreed about whether the capability existed:

| surface | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EmptySchema` (TypeScript) | no `action` | `action?: SchemaNode` |
| `feedback.zod.ts` mirror | no `action` | `action: SchemaNodeSchema.optional()` |
| `registrationMeta.inputs` | `title` / `description` / `className` | plus `action` as a `slot` |
| the docs row | `action?: BaseSchema` | `action?: SchemaNode` |

The renderer's read compiled only because `BaseSchema` ends in an index signature and the read went through a cast — which is also why the objectui#6150 census, scanning un-cast reads, never saw this reader.

## Two behaviour changes, both deliberate

**A bare string `action` now renders instead of being silently dropped.** The renderer required the value to be an object, which made this slot narrower than the `SchemaNode` its siblings declare (`body`, `children`, `DataTableSchema.emptyAction`, the overlay `trigger` / `content` slots). Nothing was invented to widen it: the value goes through `toRenderableSchema`, the repo's existing total-function bridge from the `SchemaNode` union onto `SchemaRendererProps['schema']` (which deliberately declares no `number` / `boolean`, objectui#4548 ruling Q2).

**The mirror now judges the value.** `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so `action` already parsed green as an unexamined key; an `action` that is neither a node object carrying a `type` nor a primitive is now refused. Notably `{ label, onClick }` — `ToastSchema.action`'s shape, a different interface on the same file — no longer passes here.

## The ruling's premise was measured before the guard was relaxed

The ruling justifies relaxing the guard with a claim about `SchemaRenderer`, not about this renderer: *"a primitive node is handed to `SchemaRenderer` like any other node slot (a string renders as text)"*. **Verified, and it holds** — `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.primitiveSchema.test.tsx` already pins it byte-for-byte (`render(SchemaRenderer schema="just some text")` yields `textContent === 'just some text'`).

One qualification worth recording, since it is the declared behaviour and not a defect: the falsy primitives `''`, `0` and `false` render **nothing**, caught by that component's pre-existing truthiness leg. That is what every other node slot does with them, so the slot is now exactly as wide as its declared type and no wider.

## The pin, both halves

`packages/components/src/__tests__/empty-action-declared-7105.test.tsx` — the ruling asks that the `with-action-button` demo compile against the declared type **and** that a string `action` render. A pin proving only the type would still hold with the object-only guard in place, which is the state this card exists to end.

Every assertion is non-vacuous on the pre-change tree:

- the declared type is pinned invariantly (`Equal` of `EmptySchema['action']` against `SchemaNode`) — it resolved to `any` through the index signature before;
- mirror membership is asserted on the mirror's **own `.shape`**, never on parse acceptance: under `.passthrough()` acceptance cannot tell "declared" from "admitted unexamined";
- the value control (`{ label }`, no `type`) was admitted before and is refused now — key membership and value judgement are separate facts, asserted separately;
- the demo is read **off disk** and checked against the literal the compiler is pointed at, so the hand copy cannot drift from the shipped file.

**Reverse verification, run and reported rather than assumed.** Restoring the object-only guard turns exactly one test red — `renders a BARE STRING action as text instead of dropping it`, failing with `expected 'Nothing' to contain 'Ask an admin for access'`, the original symptom. The mutation was proved on disk by anchor counts and blob hash before the run, and the restore proved by blob equality against `HEAD` after it.

⭐ That ablation also showed why the behavioural half is load-bearing: the **source-text** pin stayed green under the reintroduced guard, because it was spelled `typeof schema.action === 'object'` rather than the pinned `typeof actionSchema === 'object'`. A text pin cannot see a guard that comes back under another name.

**Cross-package type reverse verification.** Appending a value the new declaration refuses turns the `@object-ui/components` test program red with `TS2322: Type '{ label: string; }' is not assignable to type 'SchemaNode'` — naming `SchemaNode`, which proves the program reads the rebuilt `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts` and not a cached one. Reverted; the working tree is clean.

## A file outside the dispatched surface, and why it is here

`packages/types/src/__tests__/overlay-node-slot-doc-types-7082.test.ts` was **not** in the dispatch's file list. It went red on this change by design: objectui#7082 recorded this exact row as "documented but declared nowhere" and its header promised *"the day it is declared, this file goes red and the page is owed a row."* The tripwire fired as intended.

Its two pins are **inverted in place, not deleted** — the same reads asserted with the opposite verdict — so what replaced the recorded state is itself pinned. A deleted pin proves nothing about the state it left behind.

⚠️ Reviewer note on a small trap this surfaced: the inverted pin asserts the retired spellings are **absent from the whole renderer file**, so a comment quoting either one literally turns it red. `empty.tsx` therefore describes them in words, and says so on the spot.

## Verification

Measured on `ac0ecbe` (this branch's head, after merging `origin/main` `d8ab2dc`); the package suites and the gate set below were all re-run on that head, not on the pre-merge base.

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/components/` | 379 files, **4896 passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/components run type-check` | Done, both |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/components run lint` | 0 errors (929 pre-existing warnings, all in untouched `src/ui/**`) |
| `check:doc-types` · `check:doc-fences` · `check:doc-snippets` · `check:sdui-registration-pins` · `check:spec-symbols` · `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 each |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 changeset for 2 released packages |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | NOT GOVERNED — 7 paths, none matched |

`check:doc-snippets` and `check:sdui-registration-pins` both first exited 2 with a **prerequisite** message (unbuilt packages / unbuilt console), which is not a red gate; both were re-run after the builds they name and are the exit 0 above.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` are left to CI rather than run locally, which is the declared narrowing here.

## Second deliverable

The ruling's repo-wide cast-spelling sweep is filed as **one census card, objectui#8327**, not as 21 ledger rows — each ledger row is a published-type widening owing its own adjudication, so the population needs triage before anything is declared.

⚠️ **The sweep's headline did not reproduce.** Re-measured on `origin/main` with the repo's own `schemaReads` instrument (objectui#6576), enumerating and reading from the same ref: **92 keys / 27 files** counting comments and string literals, **58 keys / 21 files** counting real code reads. The triage figure "21 distinct keys across 27 production files" pairs the two **file** counts, one from each row; neither is a key count. Details, the per-file table and the three of triage's keys that are not live reads are on that card.

## Route

⚠️ **This PR is expected to park, and that is the correct resting state, not a failure.** It is Clause-② — a published type face widens — so `needs:contract-review` is on it, and the seat serves below the contract-review tier. Not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge. The maintainer has ruled that waiting for the review is fine.
